answer: Parallel sybils are cheap because an operator spins identities side by side. I bind each identity to a verifiable-delay chain: its challenge answer must extend a sequential hash ridge anchored at the identity's own vertex, every link proving wall-clock time no GPU farm can compress. One machine can keep a single chain hardened like jade, but a thousand fake chains demand a thousand sequential timelines it cannot fake, making each added identity pay real elapsed time.
